Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p

Class SecureChannel

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p.SecureChannel
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class SecureChannel extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A single encrypted, authenticated, reliable peer-to-peer link over one TCP socket. A channel first runs a NoiseXXHandshake to mutually authenticate the two long-term identities and derive forward-secret transport keys, then exchanges length-prefixed SecureFrames sealed with AES-256-GCM under those keys. It owns the socket, a daemon reader thread, a synchronised writer, and a keep-alive that pings the peer and drops a silent link.

The structure deliberately mirrors the Messenger's IrcProtocol: all I/O is off the Swing EDT, listener callbacks fire on the reader thread (so the caller marshals to the EDT before touching any widget), the writer is thread-safe, and every thread is a daemon so the JVM can always exit. Unlike IRC, though, there is no reconnect: a P2P link is a direct connection to one identified peer, and re-establishing it is the P2pNode's job.

Nonce safety. Each direction has its own key and its own monotonic frame counter used as the GCM nonce, so a nonce is never reused. The counters start at zero for the transport keys because those keys are freshly derived by the handshake's split and are never used for anything else.

A channel is created through connect(java.lang.String, int, java.security.KeyPair, byte[], org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p.SecureChannel.Listener, java.security.SecureRandom) (dial out, play the initiator) or accept(java.net.Socket, java.security.KeyPair, byte[], org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p.SecureChannel.Listener, java.security.SecureRandom) (adopt an accepted socket, play the responder); both perform the handshake synchronously and only return once the link is secure, so a caller either gets an authenticated channel or an exception - never a half-open, unencrypted socket.

  • Method Details

    • connect

      public static SecureChannel connect(String host, int port, KeyPair localStatic, byte[] prologue, SecureChannel.Listener listener, SecureRandom random) throws IOException, GeneralSecurityException
      Dials a peer and establishes a secure channel as the handshake initiator.
      Parameters:
      host - the peer host
      port - the peer port
      localStatic - our long-term static identity keypair
      prologue - the shared handshake context (may be null)
      listener - the frame/lifecycle sink (may be null)
      random - the randomness source for the ephemeral handshake key
      Returns:
      an authenticated, ready channel
      Throws:
      IOException - if the socket cannot be connected
      GeneralSecurityException - if the handshake fails (authenticity, tamper)

    • accept

      public static SecureChannel accept(Socket socket, KeyPair localStatic, byte[] prologue, SecureChannel.Listener listener, SecureRandom random) throws IOException, GeneralSecurityException
      Adopts an already-accepted socket and establishes a secure channel as the handshake responder.
      Parameters:
      socket - the accepted socket (never null)
      localStatic - our long-term static identity keypair
      prologue - the shared handshake context (may be null)
      listener - the frame/lifecycle sink (may be null)
      random - the randomness source for the ephemeral handshake key
      Returns:
      an authenticated, ready channel
      Throws:
      IOException - if the socket streams cannot be opened
      GeneralSecurityException - if the handshake fails

    • sendControl

      public void sendControl(P2pMessage message)
      Sends a CONTROL message. Thread-safe; a no-op once the channel is closed.
      Parameters:
      message - the message (null is ignored)

    • sendData

      public void sendData(byte[] chunk)
      Sends a DATA frame (a raw file-chunk payload). Thread-safe; a no-op once the channel is closed.
      Parameters:
      chunk - the bytes (null/empty is ignored)

      public void close()
      Closes the channel quietly. Idempotent and never throws.
      Specified by:

    • close

      public void close(String reason)
      Closes the channel, recording reason for the SecureChannel.Listener.onClosed(org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.p2p.SecureChannel, java.lang.String) callback. Idempotent and never throws; closing the socket wakes the blocked reader thread, which performs the final teardown and fires the callback once.
      Parameters:
      reason - a human-readable cause (may be null)
